Created attachment 3672
Patch.

When R parses an integer literal suffixed with L whose value exceeds the range of int, the function NumericValue() in src/main/gram.c performs an unchecked (int) a cast at line 4973 where a is the double result of R_atof(). If a is outside [INT_MIN, INT_MAX], this cast is undefined behavior per C11 6.3.1.4.

R already detects this case and falls back to a numeric value (the a != (double) b check at line 4978), but the UB has already occurred by line 4973 before that check runs. In practice the value of b is indeterminate after the overflow, so the comparison may or may not work depending on the compiler.

Reproducer:

parse(text = "99999999999999999999L")

Or with a hex literal:

parse(text = "0XEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEL")

Both trigger the following UBSAN diagnostic when R is built with -fsanitize=undefined:

Created attachment 3976
patch: convert integer literals to int only within the int range (gram.y + gram.c, with test)

Attachment 3672 was malformed (pasting broke it) and patched only the generated gram.c. Attached is the same change in gram.y and gram.c, against r90794: the double is cast to int only when it is within the int range, and otherwise b is NA_INTEGER, which fails the existing check, so the literal still becomes numeric with the usual warning. It also adds a regression test.

On a build with -fsanitize=float-cast-overflow, UBSan reports gram.c for the literals in the report before the patch and nothing after; make check passes.

Patch also at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/440, where CI results can be seen.
